winners.premise: A bride has a bouncer turn away the groom's fifteen-year-old son from their wedding while her own twelve-year-old daughter is welcomed inside.
winners.conflict: A father must decide whether a new marriage can begin by treating his existing child as an outsider.
winners.twist: The exclusion is not a child-free policy but the bride's attempt to define the new family without the groom's son.
winners.hook: My bride had a bouncer turn my son away from our wedding. Her own daughter was already inside.
winners.narration: Ethan texted from the door, asking where he should sit. I found him outside in the suit we'd chosen together. The bouncer said his name had been removed from the list. I told him Ethan was my son. He said the bride had given him specific instructions. I went inside and asked Claire what had happened. Her twelve-year-old daughter was waiting near the front. Claire said she didn't want reminders of my previous marriage in every photograph. We'd agreed my fifteen-year-old son would be there. She said he still had his mother, and today should be about the family we were starting. I asked whether she thought Ethan stopped being my family when I married her. She said I was twisting her words and making her daughter uncomfortable. I said neither child should be part of this argument. Then I asked her to tell the bouncer Ethan was welcome. She said if I brought him in now, everyone would know I'd chosen my old family over her. I went back outside. Ethan asked whether he'd done something wrong. I told him no, and said the wedding wasn't going ahead with him left at the door. Claire called while I was taking him to dinner. I said we'd talk later, without the children. At the restaurant, Ethan asked where he should sit. I pulled out the chair beside mine.
winners.title: The Seat Missing From Their Wedding
winners.description: The groom's son arrives in the suit they chose together. The bride has given the door staff different instructions.
winners.payoff: I pulled out the chair beside mine.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF HIS SON WAS ALREADY FAMILY

winners.premise: A father admits that he was driving drunk in the crash that killed his wife after letting their daughter blame a phone call she made for years.
winners.conflict: A father must face the cost of protecting himself with a story that made his daughter carry responsibility for her mother's death.
winners.twist: The truth may help the daughter begin to challenge her guilt, but it destroys her trust in the father offering to teach her to drive.
winners.hook: I told my daughter her call had caused the crash that killed her mum. I'd been driving drunk, but I let her apologize to me for years.
winners.narration: Leah pushed the car keys back across the table when I offered to teach her to drive. She said she'd hear that phone ringing every time she sat behind a wheel. I started saying the call had distracted us. She asked whether I still blamed a child for wanting her parents to come home. I'd accepted her apologies for years without correcting her. She asked why she should feel safe learning with me. I told her what I'd kept from her. I'd been drinking before I drove us home. Her mum had asked whether I was fit to drive. I'd said yes. Leah asked why I'd let her think a child asking for her parents was the reason her mum didn't come back. I said I'd been ashamed. She said I'd let her be ashamed instead. I tried to say I hadn't wanted to lose her too. She asked whether I'd considered the harm, or only whether she'd stay close to me. I couldn't ask her to make that easier to answer. She took the keys off the table and put them beside my hand. She said she might try lessons again, but she'd find an instructor herself. I'd wanted to be the person who helped her feel safe driving. She didn't feel safe learning from me.
winners.title: The Keys She Pushed Back Across the Table
winners.description: His daughter has blamed a phone call for her mother's death. His offer of driving lessons brings out the truth he withheld.
winners.payoff: She didn't feel safe learning from me.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF SHE DESERVED THE TRUTH

winners.premise: An assistant discovers her boss has put her photograph on an exam registration in his own name so she can earn him a qualification while remaining his unqualified assistant.
winners.conflict: An assistant must choose whether protecting her current job is worth giving her employer credit for the qualification she has studied for.
winners.twist: The boss offers to fund the exam only if the qualification belongs to him, forcing the assistant to invest in her own name instead.
winners.hook: I found my photograph on an exam registration in my boss's name. He wanted me to pass the test and keep working as his unqualified assistant.
winners.narration: Victor slid over the folder. He'd sorted out the exam fee. I asked why his name was above my picture. The business needed a qualified manager, he said, and he was the manager. I'd spent months studying after work. I asked why I couldn't take the exam as myself. He said a qualification wouldn't change my role. I should remember who'd given me a job. He opened my notes and asked me to explain the first question. I explained it. He said that was exactly why sending me made sense. I asked what happened when a client wanted the qualified person to explain the work. I'd be there to help him. I told him I wasn't sitting an exam under his name. He said if I wanted my own qualification, I could pay for it myself. I asked whether this was training support or buying an unearned certificate. He said I was making an opportunity difficult. I returned the folder and registered myself, using my holiday savings. I kept studying. When I passed, Victor asked me to leave the certificate at work for clients to see. I asked what qualified work he wanted, and what he'd pay for it. He called me his assistant again. The certificate had my photograph and my name. Neither was a mistake.
winners.title: Her Photograph Under His Name
winners.description: The assistant has done the studying. Her boss has decided whose name should receive the qualification.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF THE QUALIFICATION SHOULD BE HERS
tags: boss asks assistant to take exam

winners.premise: A wedding officiant refuses to finish a ceremony unless the bride kisses him, then tells the groom it is only a kiss.
winners.conflict: A couple must decide whether avoiding the cost and embarrassment of stopping their wedding is worth accepting the officiant's coercive demand.
winners.twist: The officiant expects the groom to pressure the bride, but the couple refuse together even though their ceremony remains unfinished.
winners.hook: Our wedding officiant wouldn't finish the ceremony unless I kissed him. He told my groom it was only a kiss.
winners.narration: He leaned toward me and said he always got the first one. I stepped back and said that wasn't happening. He smiled at the guests, then said he couldn't continue if we wouldn't respect his ceremony. I asked where he'd mentioned this before we paid him. He said couples normally understood how to have fun. Sam asked him to continue with the vows. He said Sam was making him look ridiculous. Did Sam want to disappoint everyone who'd come? Sam said that wasn't a reason to make me kiss someone. He gathered his papers. There'd be no ceremony if he left. I looked at the flowers and our families waiting. I had wanted this day for months. I asked whether he was withdrawing the demand. He said he was willing to forget the awkwardness if I gave him a quick kiss and moved on. I told him we weren't continuing with him. Sam explained to the guests exactly what he'd asked for. Nobody had been told about it before that moment. The officiant said we'd misunderstood a joke. Sam said he'd asked him twice to finish without it. We let him leave. We still had a ceremony to rearrange and money to sort out. Sam asked whether I still wanted to marry him. I said yes. Then he asked whether he could kiss me. That question made all the difference.
winners.title: The Kiss Before the Vows
winners.description: The officiant adds a condition after the guests are seated. The couple have to decide whether the ceremony can continue with him.
winners.payoff: That question made all the difference.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF A KISS NEEDS A YES
